title: Keep-Home Waiver for Sellers Who Stay with Bridgewell
content:
**Terms.** When a Real Estate Service Contracts listing order ends without a closing and the seller keeps the home under Bridgewell Homeowner Service Contracts coverage, a share of the failed-sale charge is waived. The qualifying homeowner contract is one for the same property address whose start date falls on or after the order's end date and no more than 30 calendar days after it. The waiver share is applied once, to the failed-sale charge as floored at zero, which is reduced by that share; the result is rounded to the cent.

| Seller's homeowner contract for the same property address | Monthly premium carried by that contract's tier | Share of the charge waived |
|---|---|---|
| started 0 to 30 days after the order's end date | $70.00 or more | 50% |
| started 0 to 30 days after the order's end date | below $70.00 | 25% |
| no such homeowner contract | — | no keep-home waiver |

## The start-date window counted out (hypothetical order ended on 10 May)

| Homeowner contract start date | Days after the end date | Within the window |
|---|---|---|
| 9 May | before the end date | no |
| 10 May | 0 | yes |
| 9 June | 30 | yes |
| 10 June | 31 | no |

## Records read

From the Homeowner Service Contracts records: the seller's homeowner contract for the same property address, its start date and its tier, and the monthly premium that tier carries.

## Worked example (hypothetical)

A failed-sale charge of $480.00 after its floor at zero, and a homeowner contract started 12 days after the order's end date on a tier carrying a $74.00 monthly premium: 50% waived, leaving **$240.00**. Had the tier carried a $52.00 monthly premium: 25% waived, leaving **$360.00**.
